objective: Add a ROS-free, deterministic trajectory-generator selection seam for the existing quintic and jerk-limited S-curve point-to-point planning primitives. It retains quintic as the compatibility default, accepts only exact canonical algorithm identifiers, and delegates all motion-limit validation and analytic sampling to the selected existing primitive. It neither changes the controller nor emits any robot command, simulation result, execution evidence, WorldState fact, or verification claim.
acceptance: TrajectoryAlgorithm exposes only the exact canonical strategy values quintic and s_curve.
generate_point_to_point defaults to quintic and delegates exact quintic and S-curve selections to their existing primitives without copying their limit, endpoint, or analytic-sampling logic.
Unknown, empty, case-variant, alias, and invalid-type strategy values raise ValueError without a fallback trajectory.
Both selected trajectories retain their existing immutable shared fields and analytic sample method.
The selection seam is deterministic, side-effect free, and imports no ROS, Gazebo, MuJoCo, MoveIt, hardware adapter, task runtime, public schema, event store, controller, or verifier.
Tests prove default compatibility, exact selection, deterministic behavior, fail-closed strategy validation, and propagation of the underlying explicit-limit validation.
evidence: Task Packet validation output proving the exact allowed-path boundary.
Focused uv pytest output covering delegation, determinism, and fail-closed validation.
Existing quintic and S-curve regression test output alongside strategy tests.
Repository test, contract, scenario, and context check output without any claim of Gazebo, MuJoCo, or hardware execution.
Git diff limited to the Task Packet, selection module, and its tests.
stop_conditions: Implementation requires a public contract/schema, JointController API change, ROS/Gazebo/MuJoCo/MoveIt adapter, launch/configuration, task runtime, event/replay, or hardware change.
The selection seam must infer, weaken, or duplicate the existing primitives' explicit motion-limit validation.
The implementation would fabricate observed feedback, simulator evidence, execution success, or verified task success.
Required tests or checks fail for a reason that cannot be fixed inside allowed_paths.
